claims.reason: The hypothesis can be deleted. It is an argument of the theorem: it is an instance-implicit section variable whose type mentions only q and N, both of which are already arguments, and section L2 has no `omit` for it. The statement does not need it to elaborate. In Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_GlueData.lean, `fstDiv`, `IsStrictFst` and `Divisor (AlgebraicClosure ℚ) (modularFunctionFieldBar (N * q))` all elaborate with only `[Fact q.Prime]`, `[NeZero N]`, `[Field k]` and `[CharP k q]`. The structure `PlaceSpecialization` takes only `[Fact ℓ.Prime] [NeZero N] [Field k] [CharP k ℓ]`. The definition is `fstDiv D = D.filter P.IsStrictFst`, so the statement just says that `Finsupp.filter` commutes with finite sums, which holds for any predicate. The proof uses `Finset.induction_on`, `Finsupp.filter_zero`, `Finset.sum_insert` and `fstDiv_add`. The proof of `fstDiv_add` (line 326) is `unfold PlaceSpecialization.fstDiv; exact Finsupp.filter_add` and does not use hqN. That lemma currently takes hqN as an auto-included instance argument, so it either needs `omit hqN in` as well, or the step can call `Finsupp.filter_add` directly after unfolding. Either way, the same proof works without hqN.
